svg.text: DYNAMIC TEMPLATE • MOVING ARROWS & LIVE PACKETS
Anatomy of a High-Signal Engineering Brief: The 6 Parts That Make an Agent Succeed on the First Run
Vague one-liners ('fix authentication') fail; this structure is what OpenHands, Aider, and ADK/LangGraph agents execute reliably.
ENGINEERING BRIEF #4271 — auth token expiry race
Fix the session-token expiry race so refreshes
never return a 401 inside the 60 s grace window.
One sentence, one measurable outcome. The agent plans
against this line and the verifier grades against it.
Explicit scope stops the agent from exploring 400
files and keeps the context window small (no context
A failing test first turns 'done' from an opinion into
exit_code == 0. This is the pre-completion gate.
Preserve refresh_token wire contract; no new deps;
no changes to public API signatures.
Constraints are the invariants a reviewer agent
checks; without them the fix 'works' by breaking
Run pytest + mypy + ruff in sandbox (OpenHands /
E2B); attach stdout SHA-256 receipt to the PR.
The receipt is what lets a human trust the PR in 30
A rollback line is the difference between an
autonomous merge and a 2 a.m. incident.
Rule: if the brief has no reproduction test and no proof gate, the agent is allowed to guess — and it will, on any framework.
